key_insight: GARI++ combines fast first-stage decoding with selective residual decoding to achieve accuracy competitive with state-of-the-art methods across several quantum error-correcting code families without ensembles.
engineering_relevance: The pipeline motivates hybrid FPGA–CPU decoding, pairing hardware-accelerated GARI with CPU processing of low-weight residual errors.
method: Run GARI normalized min-sum decoding with random serial scheduling on the GARI-transformed matrix.
Invoke a code-configurable second-stage decoder only when GARI does not converge, forwarding residual syndrome and soft information.
Predictively select first-stage iteration outputs expected to yield the best second-stage accuracy.
evidence_signal: At circuit-level depolarising error rate 0.001, reported FPGA GARI average latency per round spans 201 ns–11.8 µs for surface-code distances 7–25; single-core Apple M2 Union-Find residual decoding averages below 1 µs through distance 51, with accuracy on par with correlated MWPM.
watch_item: Reported component averages do not establish worst-case end-to-end latency, including FPGA–CPU communication and second-stage workload bursts.
paper_title: GARI++: A General-Purpose Decoder for Quantum Error Correction
